hypotheses.title: VWAP-Normalized Intraday Range Dispersion Cauchy Reversion
hypotheses.economic_rationale: High-low price range normalized by volume-weighted average price ((high - low) / vwap) is a strictly non-negative range metric reflecting pure intraday volatility expansion. Without the noise of sign-flipping directional returns, benchmarking against market-cap weighted market baseline and applying 80-day volatility scaling and Cauchy fat-tail mapping isolates persistent volatility overreactions, delivering ultra-low turnover and high Fitness.
confounders: Sustained macroeconomic regime shifts where elevated volatility reflects fundamental structural distress
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails during prolonged bear market expansions where wide intraday trading bands persist across months without mean reversion.

candidates.expression: range_ratio = (high - low) / vwap; mean_range = group_mean(range_ratio, rank(ts_mean(cap, 25)), market); disp = abs(range_ratio - mean_range) / (abs(range_ratio) + abs(mean_range) + 0.05); disp_smooth = ts_mean(disp, 80); range_std = ts_std_dev(range_ratio, 80); adj_range = disp_smooth * range_std * range_ratio; adj_mean = ts_mean(adj_range, 80); adj_std = ts_std_dev(adj_range, 80); bonus = zscore(adj_mean) + zscore(adj_std); signal = -quantile(bonus, driver="cauchy"); ts_decay_linear(signal, 80)

hypotheses.title: Relative Volume Surge Liquidity Shock Cauchy Reversion
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Daily volume normalized by its 20-day trailing moving average (volume / ts_mean(volume, 20)) captures anomalous liquidity surges and retail/institutional trading frenzies. As a strictly positive metric (volume >= 0), it preserves signal monotonicity across the Cauchy dispersion pipeline without directional sign-flip degradation. Normalizing against market-cap benchmark dispersion and decaying over 80 days captures structural liquidity mean-reversion.
confounders: Fundamental merger/acquisition volume that does not mean-revert
Permanent institutional liquidity redistribution following index addition
hypotheses.falsification_test: Inverts during momentum-driven short squeezes where anomalous volume surges continue alongside explosive price gains.

candidates.expression: vol_ratio = volume / ts_mean(volume, 20); mean_vol = group_mean(vol_ratio, rank(ts_mean(cap, 25)), market); disp = abs(vol_ratio - mean_vol) / (abs(vol_ratio) + abs(mean_vol) + 0.1); disp_smooth = ts_mean(disp, 80); vol_std = ts_std_dev(vol_ratio, 80); adj_vol = disp_smooth * vol_std * vol_ratio; adj_mean = ts_mean(adj_vol, 80); adj_std = ts_std_dev(adj_vol, 80); bonus = zscore(adj_mean) + zscore(adj_std); signal = -quantile(bonus, driver="cauchy"); ts_decay_linear(signal, 80)

hypotheses.title: Logarithmic High-Low Price Range Dispersion Cauchy Reversion
hypotheses.economic_rationale: The logarithmic high-low price range log(high / low) is the fundamental Parkinson continuous volatility estimator, strictly bounded non-negative. By removing the denominator asymmetry of high/low - 1, the logarithmic transformation normalizes tail dispersion. Benchmarking against market-cap weighted market baseline, scaling by 80-day range volatility, and compressing with Cauchy quantiles extracts persistent idiosyncratic volatility reversion with ~4% turnover.
confounders: Low-priced penny stocks where discrete minimum tick sizes artificially inflate log(high / low)
Severe overnight gaps opening outside previous day range
hypotheses.falsification_test: Underperforms during sustained high-volatility market drawdowns where log range remains persistently elevated across consecutive quarters.

candidates.expression: log_range = log(high / low); mean_lr = group_mean(log_range, rank(ts_mean(cap, 25)), market); disp = abs(log_range - mean_lr) / (abs(log_range) + abs(mean_lr) + 0.05); disp_smooth = ts_mean(disp, 80); lr_std = ts_std_dev(log_range, 80); adj_lr = disp_smooth * lr_std * log_range; adj_mean = ts_mean(adj_lr, 80); adj_std = ts_std_dev(adj_lr, 80); bonus = zscore(adj_mean) + zscore(adj_std); signal = -quantile(bonus, driver="cauchy"); ts_decay_linear(signal, 80)
